Frequently Asked Questions

What does Ambler do?

Ambler is a music metadata registration platform for record labels. It helps you register your releases, works, recordings, and contributor credits in one place — then delivers validated data directly to the collection societies and publishers that handle royalty payments. Ambler ensures the right information reaches the right organisations, so nothing gets lost and payments aren't delayed

Who is Ambler for?

Ambler is built for independent and mid-size record labels and the artists, songwriters, and producers they collaborate with. Whether you manage a handful of releases a year or hundreds, Ambler gives your whole team a single, shared registration workflow — so you get it right the first time, every time.

What makes Ambler different from other music registration tools?

Ambler is the only music registration platform that brings labels, artists, and contributors into one collaborative workflow. Everyone confirms their credits and splits before any data is submitted. Instead of spreadsheets, email chains, and disconnected portals, you get a single source of truth — validated, accurate, and ready for delivery.

 How do I get started with Ambler?

Getting started is simple. Sign up at useambler.io or reach out to our team and we'll walk you through the setup. You can register your first release in minutes, and your artists and contributors can join the platform for free to confirm their credits and splits.

Can my artists and contributors use Ambler?

Yes. Ambler is designed for collaboration between labels and creators. You can invite your artists, songwriters, and producers to confirm their credits and royalty splits directly on the platform — completely free of charge. Everyone stays informed, and you get validated data before anything is submitted to collection societies.

Is my data secure on Ambler?

Yes. Ambler is a GDPR-compliant platform. All data is hosted on secure infrastructure within the European Union, protected by industry-standard encryption and access controls. You remain the sole owner of your data at all times, and we never share it without your consent.
